Tallink Grupp.summary: AS Tallink Grupp has integrated ESG considerations into its core strategy and business model, completing its first double materiality assessment in 2024 and establishing corresponding KPIs and implementation strategies. The company has strengthened its ESG governance by adding dedicated FTE resources for ESG leadership and controlling, with regular ESG updates to management through bi-weekly and monthly meetings covering topics like carbon reduction, human rights, and supply chain governance. The Group's sustainability reporting follows the ESRS framework and covers material impacts across its value chain in maritime transport, hospitality, retail, and supporting services. ESG performance targets have been formalized with 62% of key suppliers having formal ESG policies in place, demonstrating the company's commitment to extending sustainability principles throughout its supply chain.

What are the company's main ESG goals?.answer: The company's main ESG goals are aligned with its overall strategy and focus on: 1) Achieving highest levels of customer satisfaction through customer safety, data protection, and human rights; 2) Developing high-quality services through sustainable supply chain relationships, environmental practices for greener service delivery, and good working conditions for employees; 3) Improving profitability and strengthening market leadership through tackling climate challenges; 4) Setting specific ESG performance targets and KPIs; and 5) Implementing formal ESG policies including carbon emission reductions, human rights, employee health, safety and well-being, and supply chain governance.

source.quote: The Group's sustainability objectives are aligned with its overall strategy, reflecting the integration of key ESG impact areas into its strategic framework

What emissions targets has the company s.answer: The company has set two main emissions targets for 2030: 1) Reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by at least 2% per annum in absolute terms (from a 2023 baseline of 423,211 tCO2e), and 2) Meet the requirements of FuelEU Maritime Regulation (from a baseline of 91.16 grams CO2e per MJ).

source.quote: Reduce the Group's Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions...Per annum reduction of at least 2% (in absolute terms)...Meet the requirements of FuelEU Maritime Regulation

How does the company approach employee w.answer: The company approaches employee wellbeing through multiple channels: ensuring employees feel valued with their voices contributing meaningfully to decisions; implementing an occupational health and safety management system where employees can submit proposals through managers and OH specialists; providing compensation for work accidents or occupational diseases including rehabilitation; collecting feedback through Employee Net Promoter Score (NPS); conducting exit interviews to identify improvement areas; and emphasizing that employee well-being is essential for delivering quality services.

source.quote: employees feel valued and that their voices contribute meaningfully to the Group's direction

What governance structures are in place.answer: The governance structures for sustainability include: GOV-2 (Information provided to and sustainability matters addressed by administrative, management and supervisory bodies), GOV-3 (Integration of sustainability-related performance in incentive schemes), GOV-4 (Statement on due diligence), and GOV-5 (Risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting). These governance elements are detailed in the Governance System section on page 24.

source.quote: GOV-2 Information provided to and sustainability matters addressed by the undertaking's administrative, management and supervisory bodies Governance System 24

What progress has been made on environme.answer: The Group has adopted a GHG Emissions Reduction Strategy focusing on actual emissions reductions from operations (over 63% from shipping operations). Short-term progress (2024-2027) includes sourcing initiatives for GHG emissions reductions. The Group will include other harmful GHG emissions (methane, nitrous oxide) beyond CO2, and will only engage in carbon offsetting with proven environmental results while avoiding greenwashing.

Eesti Energia.summary: Eesti Energia demonstrates a structured ESG approach centered on three strategic pillars: mitigating climate change through reduced environmental footprint, ensuring employee safety and management quality, and maintaining transparent governance. The company has set ambitious environmental targets including a 90% CO2 emissions reduction through carbon capture, ceasing oil shale electricity production by 2035, and achieving carbon-neutral electricity production by 2045, alongside quadrupling renewable energy capacity to 1,900 MW by 2026. The company has established robust governance structures with a strategic leadership team overseeing ESG implementation, board-level sustainability oversight, and reporting aligned with GRI and ESRS standards. Notably, no ESG-related controversies or international norm breaches have been identified for the company, and it has recently strengthened its ESG capabilities by hiring a dedicated Head of ESG.

What are the company's main ESG goals?.answer: The company's main ESG goal is to achieve carbon neutrality by capturing CO2 (reducing emissions by 90%) and adding other carbon sequestration options such as growing forests.

source.quote: Issuer will start capturing CO 2, reducing its emissions by 90% , and add other carbon sequestration options, such as growing forests, to reach carbon neutrality.

What emissions targets has the company s.answer: The company has set targets for Scope 1 GHG emissions: a 7% reduction by 2030 and a 21% reduction by 2035 compared to 2024, with the ultimate goal of achieving net zero by 2050. No targets have been set for Scopes 2 and 3.

source.quote: a 7% reduction by 2030 and a 21% reduction by 2035 compared to 2024. The ultimate goal is to achieve net zero by 2050.

How does the company approach employee w.answer: The company approaches employee wellbeing through multiple initiatives: investing in safety culture and well-being programmes, maintaining a comprehensive framework of policies based on human rights protection, fair remuneration, occupational safety and representation, and applying the ISO 45001 occupational safety standard across all subsidiaries. They regularly consult with employees on working conditions, health and safety, conduct engagement surveys, and ensure policies support both employee well-being and long-term business performance. The company also highlights flexible working arrangements and additional benefits in their motivation package as positive aspects for employee wellbeing.

source.quote: we invested in the development of our safety culture and well-being programmes

What governance structures are in place.answer: The governance structure includes: (1) A supervisory board that oversees strategic and sustainability matters, with members having competencies in energy transition, environmental management, stakeholder engagement, etc.; (2) A management board responsible for embedding sustainability in management systems and processes; (3) A sustainability steering group headed by the CFO (member of management board) who has ultimate responsibility for sustainability; (4) A sustainability manager who coordinates the steering group's activities and manages information flows; (5) Information flows from functional units through the sustainability manager and CFO to management and supervisory boards; (6) The State Assets Act and nomination committee ensure board members have necessary sustainability competencies; (7) Controls implemented per internal control framework covering data quality and audit readiness.

source.quote: The sustainability steering group is headed by the CFO, who is a member of the management board and bears ultimate responsibility for sustainability.

What progress has been made on environme.answer: Environmental initiatives have made the following progress: The company has implemented environmental action plans with specific timeframes and responsible persons, established environmental monitoring plans, and adopted a methodology for calculating GHG footprint along with a transition plan. For the 2024-2027 period, the company aims to reduce CO2 emissions to no more than 3.6 million metric tons (84% less than 1990). They are helping customers implement green transitions, increasing CO2-free energy production capacity, and have saved an estimated 1,550 metric tons of CO2 by 2027. In 2026, environmental services were restructured and transferred to business lines. The company is working toward carbon neutrality in Scope 1 emissions by 2045.

source.quote: Environmental assessment registers are used to analyse the extent to which the Group's environmental matters can be influenced and the measures that can be taken to reduce environmental impacts
